exam_set.title: Practice Set 3
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 12, Practice Set 3

questions.jp: ブラックボックステストに関する記述として、最も適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Burakku bokkusu tesuto ni kansuru kijutsu to shite, mottomo tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement about black-box testing is most appropriate?

options.label: ア
options.jp: テストデータの作成基準として、プログラムの命令や分岐に対する網羅率を使用する。
options.romaji: Tesuto dēta no sakusei kijun to shite, puroguramu no meirei ya bunki ni taisuru mōraritsu o shiyō suru.
options.en: Use statement or branch coverage as the criterion for creating test data.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 被テストプログラムに冗長なコードがあっても検出できない。
options.romaji: Hi-tesuto puroguramu ni jōchō na kōdo ga atte mo kenshutsu dekinai.
options.en: It cannot detect redundant code in the program under test.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: プログラムの内部構造に着目し、必要な部分が実行されたかどうかを検証する。
options.romaji: Puroguramu no naibu kōzō ni chakumoku shi, hitsuyō na bubun ga jikkō sareta ka dō ka o kenshō suru.
options.en: Focus on internal program structure and verify that required parts were executed.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 分岐命令やモジュールの数が増えると、テストデータが急増する。
options.romaji: Bunki meirei ya mojūru no kazu ga fueru to, tesuto dēta ga kyūzō suru.
options.en: Test data increases rapidly as the number of branches and modules increases.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Black-box testing checks inputs and outputs without opening the program to inspect its code. Hidden unused code can therefore remain unnoticed.

Technical breakdown:
Black-box test cases come from specifications, using methods such as equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis. Because internal statements and branches are not examined, redundant or unreachable code may produce no visible failure and cannot reliably be detected.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ブラックボックステスト = burakku bokkusu tesuto = black-box testing
冗長なコード = jōchō na kōdo = redundant code
内部構造 = naibu kōzō = internal structure

Why the best solution works:
イ states a real limitation caused by ignoring implementation internals.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Statement and branch coverage are white-box criteria based on internal structure.
ウ:
Inspecting internal structure and execution coverage defines white-box testing.
エ:
Branch-count-driven test growth is associated with structural white-box coverage, not the defining behavior of black-box testing.

Memory trick:
Black box sees behavior, not hidden code.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 流れ図において、判定条件網羅（分岐網羅）を満たす最少のテストケース数は幾つか。流れ図の第1判定は「X＞1」で、真の場合は「（X÷2）→X」を実行する。第2判定は「A＝2 or B＝0」で、真の場合は「（X＋1）→X」を実行する。
questions.romaji: Nagarezu ni oite, hantei jōken mōra (bunki mōra) o mitasu saisū no tesuto kēsu-sū wa ikutsu ka. Nagarezu no daiichi hantei wa 'X dai nari ichi' de, shin no baai wa '(X waru ni) ya-jirushi X' o jikkō suru. Daini hantei wa 'A ikōru ni or B ikōru zero' de, shin no baai wa '(X purasu ichi) ya-jirushi X' o jikkō suru.
questions.en: In the flowchart, what is the minimum number of test cases needed for decision/branch coverage? The first decision is X > 1 and, if true, assigns X ÷ 2 to X. The second is A = 2 or B = 0 and, if true, assigns X + 1 to X.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Each decision must say yes once and no once. Two carefully chosen runs can do that for both decisions.

Technical breakdown:
Decision coverage requires every decision result, true and false, at least once. Test case 1 can make X > 1 true and A = 2 or B = 0 true. Test case 2 can make X > 1 false and A = 2 or B = 0 false. Thus both outcomes of both decision nodes are covered with 2 tests. One test cannot make the same decision both true and false, so 2 is also the minimum.

Japanese keywords to remember:
判定条件網羅 = hantei jōken mōra = decision coverage
分岐網羅 = bunki mōra = branch coverage
最少 = saisū = minimum

Why the best solution works:
イ provides the minimum pair of complementary executions needed to cover true and false branches.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
One execution selects only one outcome at each decision and cannot cover both branches.
ウ:
Three tests can achieve coverage but are not the minimum.
エ:
Four tests are unnecessary because outcomes of the two decisions can be paired in two runs.

Memory trick:
Branch coverage: each diamond needs T and F; two runs can pair them.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 図の構造をもつプログラムに対して、ホワイトボックステストのテストケースを設計するとき、少なくとも実施しなければならないテストケース数が最大になるテスト技法はどれか。図の判定条件は「A＞0 かつ B＝1」で、真の場合に「X←X＋1」を実行する。
questions.romaji: Zu no kōzō o motsu puroguramu ni taishite, howaito bokkusu tesuto no tesuto kēsu o sekkei suru toki, sukunakutomo jisshi shinakereba naranai tesuto kēsu-sū ga saidai ni naru tesuto gihō wa dore ka. Zu no hantei jōken wa 'A dai nari zero katsu B ikōru ichi' de, shin no baai ni 'X hidari-yajirushi X purasu ichi' o jikkō suru.
questions.en: For the shown program, which white-box method requires the greatest minimum number of test cases? The decision is A > 0 AND B = 1, and when true it executes X ← X + 1.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
The strictest method tries every true/false combination of the two small conditions, so it needs the most tests.

Technical breakdown:
The decision contains two atomic conditions: C1 = A > 0 and C2 = B = 1. Multiple-condition coverage tests all 2² = 4 combinations: TT, TF, FT, and FF. Condition coverage can cover each atomic condition true and false in 2 tests; decision coverage needs true and false decision outcomes, also achievable in 2; statement coverage needs the X increment executed at least once, achievable in 1. Therefore the largest minimum is 4.

Japanese keywords to remember:
複数条件網羅 = fukusū jōken mōra = multiple-condition coverage
条件網羅 = jōken mōra = condition coverage
命令網羅 = meirei mōra = statement coverage

Why the best solution works:
ウ requires every combination of both atomic conditions, producing 2² = 4 cases.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Condition coverage requires each atomic condition true and false, but not every combination; 2 cases can suffice.
イ:
Decision coverage needs the whole expression true and false; 2 cases suffice.
エ:
Statement coverage only needs the increment statement executed, so 1 true case suffices.

Memory trick:
Multiple conditions: n booleans mean 2ⁿ combinations.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: 流れ図で表される部分を命令網羅によってテストするとき、テストケースは少なくとも幾つ用意する必要があるか。第1判定は「a＝0」で、Yesの場合は「x＝1」、Noの場合は「x＝2」を実行する。続く第2判定は「b＝0」で、Yesの場合は「y＝1」、Noの場合は「y＝2」を実行する。
questions.romaji: Nagarezu de arawasareru bubun o meirei mōra ni yotte tesuto suru toki, tesuto kēsu wa sukunakutomo ikutsu yōi suru hitsuyō ga aru ka. Daiichi hantei wa 'a ikōru zero' de, Yes no baai wa 'x ikōru ichi', No no baai wa 'x ikōru ni' o jikkō suru. Tsuzuku daini hantei wa 'b ikōru zero' de, Yes no baai wa 'y ikōru ichi', No no baai wa 'y ikōru ni' o jikkō suru.
questions.en: When testing the shown flowchart with statement coverage, what is the minimum number of test cases? The first decision a = 0 executes x = 1 for Yes or x = 2 for No. The second decision b = 0 executes y = 1 for Yes or y = 2 for No.
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Every assignment box must run at least once. One run can take both Yes branches; another can take both No branches.

Technical breakdown:
Statement coverage requires x = 1, x = 2, y = 1, and y = 2 each to execute. Case 1: a = 0 and b = 0 executes x = 1 and y = 1. Case 2: a ≠ 0 and b ≠ 0 executes x = 2 and y = 2. All four statements are covered in 2 cases. A single case cannot execute both alternatives of either decision, so 2 is minimal.

Japanese keywords to remember:
命令網羅 = meirei mōra = statement coverage
流れ図 = nagarezu = flowchart
用意する = yōi suru = prepare

Why the best solution works:
ア pairs the Yes outcomes in one run and No outcomes in another, covering every assignment with the minimum 2 tests.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Three cases cover the statements but include an unnecessary extra execution.
ウ:
Four cases test all combinations of the two decisions, which exceeds statement-coverage requirements.
エ:
Five cases add further redundancy and are not minimal.

Memory trick:
Statement coverage asks whether every box ran, not every path.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: ボトムアップテストの特徴として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Botomu appu tesuto no tokuchō to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which is an appropriate characteristic of bottom-up testing?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 開発の初期の段階では、並行作業が困難である。
options.romaji: Kaihatsu no shoki no dankai de wa, heikō sagyō ga konnan de aru.
options.en: Parallel work is difficult in the early development stage.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: テスト済みの上位モジュールが必要である。
options.romaji: Tesuto-zumi no jōi mojūru ga hitsuyō de aru.

options.label: エ
options.jp: ドライバが必要である。

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Bottom-up testing starts with low-level modules. A temporary caller is needed to tell those modules what to do.

Technical breakdown:
Low-level modules are integrated and tested before their real upper-level callers exist. A driver simulates an upper module by invoking the module under test and supplying inputs. Stubs instead simulate lower modules in top-down testing.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ボトムアップテスト = botomu appu tesuto = bottom-up testing
ドライバ = doraiba = driver
上位モジュール = jōi mojūru = upper-level module

Why the best solution works:
エ supplies the missing caller needed to exercise a lower-level module during bottom-up integration.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Bottom-up work can be divided among lower modules and does not inherently prevent parallel development.
イ:
Stubs replace lower modules and are mainly required for top-down testing.
ウ:
Real tested upper modules are not required because drivers stand in for them.

Memory trick:
Bottom needs a driver above to call it.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: トップダウン方式で結合テストを行うとき、特に必要となるものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Toppu daun hōshiki de ketsugō tesuto o okonau toki, toku ni hitsuyō to naru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: What is especially necessary when performing integration testing with the top-down method?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Top-down testing starts at the top while some lower modules are missing, so small fake lower modules stand in for them.

Technical breakdown:
The upper control modules are integrated first. A stub has the same callable interface as an unfinished lower module and returns controlled results, allowing the upper flow and interfaces to be tested. Drivers are used for the opposite bottom-up direction.

Japanese keywords to remember:
トップダウン方式 = toppu daun hōshiki = top-down method
結合テスト = ketsugō tesuto = integration testing
スタブ = sutabu = stub

Why the best solution works:
イ replaces unavailable subordinate modules called by the upper modules under test.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
An emulator reproduces another machine or environment, not a missing subordinate module interface.
ウ:
A debugger helps inspect execution but does not replace an unfinished module.
エ:
A driver simulates an upper caller and is used in bottom-up testing.

Memory trick:
Top calls down to stubs.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 階層構造のモジュール群から成るソフトウェアの結合テストを、上位のモジュールから行う。この場合に使用する、下位のモジュールの代替となるテスト用のモジュールはどれか。
questions.romaji: Kaisō kōzō no mojūru-gun kara naru sofutowea no ketsugō tesuto o, jōi no mojūru kara okonau. Kono baai ni shiyō suru, kai no mojūru no daitai to naru tesuto-yō no mojūru wa dore ka.
questions.en: Integration testing of hierarchical software starts from upper modules. Which test module substitutes for a lower module?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
When the top module calls a lower module that is not ready, a stub pretends to be that lower module.

Technical breakdown:
In top-down integration, a stub implements the called interface of a missing subordinate module with simplified, predictable behavior. This lets testers verify control flow and interface usage from the upper level before the real lower component is complete.

Japanese keywords to remember:
上位のモジュール = jōi no mojūru = upper-level module
下位のモジュール = kai no mojūru = lower-level module
代替 = daitai = substitute

Why the best solution works:
ウ is the standard test double used in place of a called lower-level module.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
An emulator imitates another hardware or execution environment.
イ:
A simulator models behavior of a system or process but is not the standard integration-test substitute named here.
エ:
A driver replaces an upper caller when testing from the bottom upward.

Memory trick:
Stub stands below; driver calls from above.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: モジュール間やサブシステム間のインタフェースを検証するために行うテストはどれか。
questions.romaji: Mojūru-kan ya sabushisutemu-kan no intafēsu o kenshō suru tame ni okonau tesuto wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which test verifies interfaces between modules or between subsystems?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Integration testing checks whether separately built pieces connect and communicate correctly.

Technical breakdown:
After individual modules pass unit testing, they are combined. Integration testing verifies calls, parameters, data formats, return values, timing, and control transfer across module or subsystem boundaries.

Japanese keywords to remember:
結合テスト = ketsugō tesuto = integration testing
インタフェース = intafēsu = interface
モジュール間 = mojūru-kan = between modules

Why the best solution works:
イ targets defects that appear only when components exchange data or control through their interfaces.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Operational testing checks suitability in the real user and operating environment.
ウ:
System testing verifies the complete system against system requirements.
エ:
Unit testing checks an individual module in isolation.

Memory trick:
Integration = test the joins.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 運用テストにおける検査内容として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Un'yō tesuto ni okeru kensa naiyō to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which inspection item is appropriate in operational testing?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 個々のソフトウェアユニットについて、仕様を満足していることを確認する。
options.romaji: Koko no sofutowea yunitto ni tsuite, shiyō o manzoku shite iru koto o kakunin suru.
options.en: Confirm that each software unit satisfies its specification.

options.label: イ
options.jp: ソフトウェア品目の中で使用しているアルゴリズムの妥当性を確認する。
options.romaji: Sofutowea hinmoku no naka de shiyō shite iru arugorizumu no datōsei o kakunin suru.
options.en: Confirm the validity of algorithms used within the software item.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: ソフトウェアユニット間のインタフェースが整合していることを確認する。
options.romaji: Sofutowea yunitto-kan no intafēsu ga seigō shite iru koto o kakunin suru.
options.en: Confirm that interfaces between software units are consistent.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 利用者に提供するという視点で、システムが要求を満足していることを確認する。
options.romaji: Riyōsha ni teikyō suru to iu shiten de, shisutemu ga yōkyū o manzoku shite iru koto o kakunin suru.
options.en: From the viewpoint of providing the system to users, confirm that it satisfies requirements.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Operational testing asks whether the finished system truly works for users in the environment where they will use it.

Technical breakdown:
Operational or acceptance-oriented testing validates the complete system from the user and business-operation viewpoint. It checks required functions, workflows, usability, operating procedures, and readiness for actual service rather than isolated code details.

Japanese keywords to remember:
運用テスト = un'yō tesuto = operational testing
利用者 = riyōsha = user
要求を満足する = yōkyū o manzoku suru = satisfy requirements

Why the best solution works:
エ evaluates the delivered system against user requirements from the service-provision viewpoint.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Checking each software unit against its specification is unit testing.
イ:
Inspecting algorithm validity is a unit-level or review concern.
ウ:
Checking interfaces between software units is integration testing.

Memory trick:
Operational test: can real users run the real system?

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: ソフトウェアのテストの種類のうち、ソフトウェア保守のために行った変更によって、影響を受けないはずの箇所に影響を及ぼしていないかどうかを確認する目的で行うものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Sofutowea no tesuto no shurui no uchi, sofutowea hoshu no tame ni okonatta henkō ni yotte, eikyō o ukenai hazu no kasho ni eikyō o oyoboshite inai ka dō ka o kakunin suru mokuteki de okonau mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which test checks whether a maintenance change has unintentionally affected areas that should not have been affected?

options.label: エ
options.jp: リグレッションテスト

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
After fixing one part, rerun earlier tests to make sure the fix did not break something that used to work.

Technical breakdown:
Software changes can cause side effects in unchanged components through shared data, dependencies, interfaces, or control flow. Regression testing repeats relevant existing tests after a change to detect such unintended deterioration while also confirming preserved behavior.

Japanese keywords to remember:
リグレッションテスト = riguresshon tesuto = regression testing
ソフトウェア保守 = sofutowea hoshu = software maintenance
影響を及ぼす = eikyō o oyobosu = affect

Why the best solution works:
エ is specifically designed to detect new defects introduced into previously correct behavior by modifications.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Operational testing checks readiness and suitability in actual use.
イ:
Integration testing focuses on interfaces among combined components.
ウ:
System testing verifies the whole system against system requirements, but the change-related recheck described is specifically regression testing.

Memory trick:
Regression means a change made old behavior go backward.

Correct answer: エ
